stats.fact: MobARK is Apache-2.0 licensed, requires Python 3.11+ and Node 18+
MobARK repo created 2026-08-12; latest release v0.3.0 dated 2026-08-21
MobARK runs as four containers under docker compose: app, worker, redis, and searxng
Static analysis stack: jadx + apktool (Android decompile), semgrep (curated + OWASP MASTG rules), gitleaks (secrets), LIEF (iOS Mach-O)
AI Agent uses a local LLM (Ollama / LM Studio) or BYOK provider; opt-in web research via bundled SearXNG (SSRF-guarded, HTTP JSON only)
Edit & recompile (Android smali) is amd64-only because it needs Google Android build-tools (zipalign/apksigner) and apktool aapt2, which are Linux x86_64-only
iOS stays read-only: rebuilding an IPA requires an Apple Developer account and signing certificates
Reports are deterministic Markdown/PDF with banded risk-index scoring (high | warning | info), per-finding suppression, and AI or no-model explanations
Auth: username/password (stdlib scrypt) + GitHub/Google OAuth; first registered account becomes instance admin; per-user data isolation and encrypted per-user key vault (scrypt KEK + AES-GCM)
MobSF (main open-source alternative) has 21,702 stars and 3,760 forks and supports Android, iOS, and Windows Mobile with static + dynamic analysis

angles: MobARK is a very new (Aug 2026) self-hosted mobile appsec platform that differentiates via a built-in AI Agent that chats with decompiled code through a local LLM — a privacy-first alternative to cloud MAST tools
Privacy/self-hosting angle: nothing leaves your infrastructure by default; the only outbound traffic is opt-in agent web research — key for security teams that can't upload binaries to third parties
AI Agent as differentiator: chat-with-decompiled-code, tool-calling, live step/token streaming, opt-in SearXNG web research — vs MobSF which has no built-in LLM agent
Android edit & recompile workflow (smali edits, resigned test APK builds) enables validation loops, but is amd64-only and iOS stays read-only — a real limitation to call out
Maturity caveat: 21 stars / 1 fork and v0.3.0 within weeks of creation means it's early-stage; dynamic analysis is still on the roadmap — honest review should flag production-readiness
Comparison angle: MobARK vs MobSF vs commercial MAST (Edgescan, AppKnox) — where each fits for pentesters, DevSecOps, and privacy-sensitive orgs
